results.summary: Moved this to Bonanza Peak as the Northwest Ridge (from Needle Peak), V 5.8, because it describes a two-day traverse that finishes on Bonanza, and Needle's own north ridge is the other Needle row.
results.evidence: The AAJ report is titled 'Bonanza Peak, Northwest Ridge' and describes one new route (V 5.8) on Bonanza: Needle Peak by its north ridge, first ascents of the Anonymity Towers at low 5th, Dark Glacier and Dark Peak, the crest to Bonanza's west and main summits (5.8 on the last two pitches), descent by the Mary Green Glacier. A later account of the Dark-Bonanza traverse (July 2017) rates it 5.8+, mostly 4th and low 5th on a long knife-edge ridge above glaciers, which confirms the line as a Bonanza route. None of Bonanza's six rows (Mary Green Glacier, Northeast Buttress, Soviet Route, North Ridge, Cascadian Route, Oregonian Route) is this line, so no duplicate. The row's beta misspelled 'Haider' as 'Halder'. Season set to Jul-Aug from the August and July ascents; 'single documented ascent' wording dropped.

ops.value: Bonanza Peak's Northwest Ridge (V 5.8) is a long, rarely repeated link-up that reaches Washington's highest non-volcanic summit from the northwest. This version starts from Swamp Creek off the Agnes Creek trail: it climbs Needle Peak by its north ridge, carries over the North and South Anonymity Towers at low fifth class, crosses the Dark Glacier to Dark Peak, and then follows the high, knife-edged crest joining Dark Peak to Bonanza's west and main summits, with the hardest climbing (5.8) on the last two pitches. It descends the Mary Green Glacier toward Holden.

Guye Peak's steep, sun-exposed West Face rises directly above the Alpental valley and is one of the most visible alpine rock walls from I-90 at Snoqualmie Pass. It holds several moderate multi-pitch lines on generally featured but often dirty and loose Cascade rock, following discontinuous ramp and slab systems up to the summit ridge; the best-known specific line on this face is the Improbable Traverse. A November 2021 rockfall event stripped a large section of rock from the face and buried lower pitches in dirt and debris, changing conditions from older route descriptions.
ops.value: Guye Peak's west face rises above the Alpental valley at Snoqualmie Pass. This is its easiest line and a short, close-to-the-road alpine outing: from the north end of the talus it follows a huge tree-covered ramp that climbs across the whole face from north to south, then a short step of Class 4 to low fifth onto a second grassy ramp, and a final low-fifth crack and face that eases through rock and alpine trees to the south summit. The rock is often dirty and loose. The harder Improbable Traverse on the same face is a separate climb.

results.evidence: The AAJ (pub. 1988) North Face note by Burdo: four pitches up the central chimney (probably the melted-out Kloke-Simon route), three on an exposed rib, a gully of monstrous chockstones, IV 5.10, about 4,000 ft. The NWMJ 2005 note: Northeast Face Couloir (Kloke-Simon, July 1976), winter ascent 13 Mar 2005 by Taylor and Miller: bivy at 4,000 ft at the glacier foot, lower rock band mid-fifth in summer, snowfield traverse, crux iced slabs and a steep chockstone, upper couloir to the ridge at about 6,700 ft. A separate listing names the Burdo-Cairns route on the NE face as distinct from the Kloke-Simon couloir. The two climbs share the chimney/couloir in part, but they are recorded as separate routes with different grades. Adjustments: the approach column (the Burdo account's vague cirque note) moves to the new row and this row gets the 2005 approach its itinerary already describes; gain_ft 4000 and length_m 930 are cleared here because they come from the Burdo climbing figure or from no source; the FA year is given as 1974 or 1976; the Burdo year is left out because the note does not state it (publication 1988).

new_row.name: North Face
new_row.overview: A serious, rarely-repeated alpine rock route up Davis Peak's huge north-facing cirque wall: four pitches up a prominent central chimney system, then three pitches out onto an exposed rib of delicate face climbing, finishing through a gully choked with large chockstones to the summit.
new_row.beta: The route climbs the northern cirque by its prominent central chimney system for four pitches, then exits left onto an exposed rib for three pitches of delicate face climbing before re-entering a gully choked with very large chockstones that leads to the top near the summit. The chimney is probably a melted-out form of the older Kloke-Simon couloir line. About 4,000 ft of climbing; part of the first ascent was done by moonlight.

ops.expect: A serious, rarely-repeated alpine rock route up Davis Peak's huge north-facing cirque wall: four pitches up a prominent central chimney system, then three pitches out onto an exposed rib of delicate face climbing, finishing through a gully choked with large chockstones to the summit.
ops.value: The Northeast Face Couloir climbs Davis Peak's huge northeast wall above Stetattle Creek, one of the biggest faces in the North Cascades: a compact lower rock band, a traverse left across a large snowfield, belayed crux pitches over iced slabs and a steep chockstone, then a long, exposed upper couloir to the cornices where it meets the summit ridge near 6,700 ft. It goes in summer as a rock-and-snow route and has been climbed in winter; the descent is the long south side.

ops.expect: First climbed by Andy Cairns and Bryan Burdo (Affiliated Climbers of the Montlake Erratic). The route climbs the northern cirque via a central chimney system — possibly a melted-out variant of an earlier 1974 Kloke-Simon line — for four pitches, then exits left onto an exposed rib for three pitches of delicate face climbing, before re-entering a gully with large ('monstrous') chockstones leading to the summit. Part of the first ascent was done by moonlight.
ops.value: From a bivouac at about 4,000 ft at the foot of the glacier, climb the glacier to the bergschrund and simul-climb the compact lower rock band (mid-fifth class in summer, hard to protect) to the right side of the large snowfield. Traverse left across the snowfield to the couloir, belay the crux pitches over iced slabs and a steep chockstone, and continue up the long, exposed upper couloir to the cornices where it meets the summit ridge at about 6,700 ft. The summit is a short way along the ridge.

ops.expect: Approached via Davis Peak's northern cirque, gained from the Gorge Creek/Stetattle Creek drainages north of the peak; beyond that the first-ascent account gives no detailed trailhead-to-base mileage.
ops.value: From Diablo, take the Stetattle Creek trail about 2 mi, drop about 200 ft to ford the creek opposite Davis Peak, then bushwhack and scramble a Class 3-4 rib, roping up for slabby sections, through slide alder above the cliffs to flat ground at the toe of the glacier, about 4,000 ft. Expect roughly eight or nine hours from the road. The Stetattle Creek trail is currently closed for post-fire hazards.
